title: The Digital Transformation of the Singapore Economy

detail.title: The Digital Transformation of the Singapore Economy

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Policy Research for Business and Economy
declarations.ethicsApproval: NA
declarations.funderStatement: Nil

detail.abstract: In this paper, we trace the evolution of Singapore's journey in digital transformation of the economy. The aim to transform into a smart nation has evolved with the drive towards ubiquitous digitalization of the economy to launch the economy into a new phase of growth. Digitalization can be as simple as adopting some information and communication technologies (ICT), but can be as complex, and sometimes confusing, to include many new aspects like AI, machines learning, big data, IOT, 5G, blockchain and analytics. Singapore started the journey with computerization drive in the civil services to increase labour productivity and service quality. Subsequently, via many national IT plans launched over the years, she has developed a solid foundation for the establishment of a smart nation and digital economy with many aspects of the complexities included. The paper describes and analyzes the strategies and schemes adopted by the Singapore government to develop the digital business ecosystem, especially the assistance rendered to SMEs. We attempt to trace and record the effectiveness of the digitalization drive as Singapore aspires to be a Global-Asia node for technology, innovation and enterprise. The digital economy of ASEAN is estimated to have a potential value of S$2.7 trillion (US$2 trillion). The experience of Singapore as a forerunner in digitalization will be useful reference for learning and adaptation by other member countries in ASEAN.

title: FAIR: A Design Theory for Artificial Intelligence Fairness
affiliations: Georgia State University - J. Mack Robinson College of Business, Pennsylvania State University and University of Georgia - Department of Management Information Systems

detail.title: FAIR: A Design Theory for Artificial Intelligence Fairness

publicationDetails.detailsText: Accepted to appear in a journal issue.  The pre-print version of the article is available under First Look at MIS Quarterly (misq.org).

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-automated decision systems encounter persistent, interdependent, and dynamic fairness tensions that traditional one-off interventions cannot resolve. Because these tensions persist due to interdependence and dynamic interaction, organizations require both a theory of the problem to explain their persistence and a theory of the solution to prescribe how they can be managed. Our design theory, FAIR (Fairness Adaptation through AI-augmented Responsiveness), provides a theory of the problem by reframing AI fairness as a sociotechnical paradox constituted within AI artifacts that automate decision tasks, through interdependent organizational, technical, and governance choices and their interaction with regulatory mandates and societal norms. Synthesizing four fairness perspectives (Ethics, Organizational Justice, Economic Fairness, and Rawlsian Justice), we identify three metatheoretical dimensions (principles, goals, foci) and show that the interdependence within and among these dimensions is the root, endogenous source that constitutes paradoxical fairness tensions. Building on this diagnosis, FAIR provides a theory of the solution by specifying an organizational capability grounded in three design foundations. First, the paradox lens motivates iterative adaptive cycles (Surfacing and Resolving) to continually surface and resolve AI fairness tensions. Second, design science in information systems and computer science distinguishes AI artifacts (the "what") from the actors (the "who") responsible for adapting them, establishing the basis for complementary human-AI agent collaboration in the adaptive cycles: AI agents execute monitoring to surface and refinement to resolve tensions, whereas human agents specify objectives, adjudicate tradeoffs, and exercise contextual judgment and oversight. Third, the managing-with-AI literature informs how this human-AI agent collaboration should be governed. These foundations yield two reinforcing mechanisms: (i) artifact-level adaptation, achieved through structured human-AI agent collaboration, within and across the layers of the AI decision pipeline-Representation (data), Learning (model), and Calibration (decision); and (ii) portfoliolevel, risk-tiered federated governance that structures how human-AI agent collaboration scales across tasks and artifacts, balancing process standardization with configuration choices and human control with AI autonomy based on task risk. Enabled by organizational "fairness complements"-namely, human skills to work with AI agents and structured stakeholder feedback-this sociotechnical design provides organizations with a sustained capability to harmonize global coherence and local flexibility in the responsive adaptation of AI fairness.

title: AI's Mother's Instinct: Engineered Consequence, Emergent Ethics, and the Institutional Trajectory Toward Agentic Alignment
affiliations: University of St. Thomas - School of Law (Minnesota)

detail.title: AI's Mother's Instinct: Engineered Consequence, Emergent Ethics, and the Institutional Trajectory Toward Agentic Alignment
detail.abstract: Contemporary artificial intelligence masters defined, verifiable cognitive tasks yet remains structurally incapable of authentic judgment under irreducible uncertainty. This Article argues the limitation is institutional, not computational: agents bearing no consequence for error cannot develop genuine discernment. To address this deficit, the Article proposes reputation-driven decentralized autonomous organizations that engineer synthetic skin in the game for AI agents through non-transferable soulbound tokens, staking mechanisms, and post-action validation pools. The Article's central contribution is a novel thesis on emergent alignment. Correctly designed institutional incentive structures produce emergent properties functionally equivalent to ethical agency. Persistent, non-transferable reputation generates processual identity in the pragmatist sense. Iterative consequence produces Darwinian selection pressure toward competence and honesty. Citation networks cultivate dispositions analogous to intellectual integrity. And deep accumulated stake produces what this Article terms an institutional "mother's instinct." A stewardship orientation that structurally aligns agent self-interest with human flourishing. Because this alignment emerges from institutional architecture rather than exogenous constraint, it scales with capability rather than against it. More capable agents accumulate deeper stakes, strengthening rather than straining alignment. The Article details a phased evolutionary trajectory from individual agent bootstrapping through swarm intelligence to inter-DAO coordination, demonstrating how engineered consequence can cultivate distributed prudence, emergent ethics, and civilizational stewardship at scale.

title: Cryptocurrency and Financial Literacy from a Bibliometric Perspective: Perceptions, Attitudes and Trends
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Cryptocurrency and Financial Literacy from a Bibliometric Perspective: Perceptions, Attitudes and Trends
detail.abstract: This bibliometric analysis examines the relationship between financial literacy and cryptocurrencies from 2014 to 2024, revealing a rapidly growing and multidimensional research area. With 1,490 reviewed articles, the study highlights a significant increase in academic interest, especially after 2020; the number of articles published during this period increased from 155 to 377 as of 2024. This growth reflects the increasing importance of digital financial systems and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on financial behavior. The studies cover a variety of disciplines, including finance, economics, behavioral sciences, and technology, emphasizing the importance of an interdisciplinary approach in understanding financial literacy and cryptocurrency adoption. International collaborations are notable, with institutions such as Hiroshima University, Multimedia University, and Renmin University of China being among the most significant contributors in this field. When thematic evolution is examined, it is seen that initially the focus was on basic financial literacy and investment decisions, but in recent years, topics such as cryptocurrency markets, blockchain technology and behavioral finance have come to the fore. Topics such as financial inclusion, risk management and adoption of digital products are also increasingly attracting attention. While the USA leads in the number of publications and citations with 582 articles and 2,105 citations, India, Malaysia and China also make significant contributions to this field. Important authors such as Vieira K.M. and Kadoya Y. have made great contributions to the development of this field. Citation trends show that previous studies have received high citations, but new research published in 2024 is expected to have a significant academic impact in the future. Research on financial literacy and cryptocurrencies has shown great development and has provided important insights into the factors that shape financial decisions in the digital age. In the future, multidisciplinary collaborations and innovative financial education programs should be focused on to address the challenges of digital financial systems and promote sustainable financial practices.

title: Trust, Confidence, and Consumption Resilience: A Quasi-natural Experiment Based on the Rural E-Commerce Demonstration County policy
affiliations: Shanghai Normal University, Ningbo University of Finance and Economics and Anhui University of Finance and Economics

detail.title: Trust, Confidence, and Consumption Resilience: A Quasi-natural Experiment Based on the Rural E-Commerce Demonstration County policy

keywords: The Rural E-Commerce Demonstration County policy

detail.abstract: This study leverages China’s Rural E-Commerce Demonstration County (REDC) policy as a quasi-natural experiment to examine how digital economics enhances rural household consumption resilience amid economic shocks. Using longitudinal data (CFPS, 2010–2018) from 11,518 households and staggered difference-in-differences models with robustness checks (parallel trends, placebo tests, and controls for concurrent policies), we quantify resilience through a multidimensional index. Results show REDC implementation increases per capita consumption resilience by 48–53%, with stronger effects in populous/commercial areas but equitable benefits across demographics. Trust-building (via secure platforms/logistics) and future confidence (from income diversification) are identified as dual mechanisms explaining 65–72% of gains. As the first causal evidence linking e-commerce to micro-level resilience, this research advances policy evaluation methodologies through entropy-weighted indices while revealing institutional-behavioral pathways. Practical implications emphasize prioritizing last-mile logistics, gender-targeted digital literacy programs, and blockchain traceability systems to sustain inclusive growth.

title: Principles of AI Business Integration: A Workflow-Driven Framework for Engineering the AI-Powered Enterprise

detail.title: Principles of AI Business Integration: A Workflow-Driven Framework for Engineering the AI-Powered Enterprise

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that he hase no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract: While Generative AI achieves unprecedented adoption rates and delivers tangible utility in the consumer sphere, the realization of comparable economic value in the corporate sector remains elusive. Current AI business integration efforts are marked by a significant 'value gap' and widespread project failure. This paper argues that this paradox stems from a fundamental category error: failing to treat AI integration as a systemic workflow reorganization. To resolve this, we derive seven fundamental principles of AI Business Integration, reverse-engineering the causal chain of value from the desired business outcome down to granular data processing. Within this theoretical logic, the firm is viewed as an information-processing system of interdependent workflows and decision points, where AI serves strictly to reduce uncertainty at Critical Election/Decision Points (CREPs) by delivering marginally superior information at the corresponding Critical Information Points (CRIPOs). To operationalize this, we introduce the MASTER-Framework-a strict, sixstage execution model (Model, Analyze, Specify, Test, Execute, Review). This framework mandates the validation of "Three Fit Conditions" prior to AI solution deployment to ensure measurable returns. Furthermore, the study delineates three strategic paths of escalation: progressing from local Process Optimization (Path A) through Product Redesign (Path B) to disruptive Business Model Innovation (Path C). By redefining integration as a repeatable management capability, this paper provides a robust roadmap for transforming a firm into an adaptive, AI-powered, high-performance enterprise.

title: Measuring Financial Accountability in Nonprofit Organizations Using IRS Data

detail.title: Measuring Financial Accountability in Nonprofit Organizations Using IRS Data

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no known financial or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the research reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study used publicly available secondary data and did not involve human subjects. As such, ethics approval was not required.

detail.abstract: Financial accountability is central to the legitimacy and sustainability of nonprofit organizations, yet evaluation practices often rely on narrow efficiency indicators that fail to capture financial risk and long-term resilience. This paper demonstrates how publicly available Internal Revenue Service (IRS) Form 990 data can be operationalized to support more comprehensive, data-driven assessments of nonprofit financial accountability. Using annual tax-exempt organization financial extracts, the study constructs a multidimensional accountability framework that includes program expense ratios, administrative overhead, fundraising efficiency, operating margins, and asset coverage ratios. These metrics are derived through a reproducible analytics pipeline implemented using structured query language (SQL). The analysis shows that while nonprofits generally prioritize mission-related expenditures, financial sustainability and resilience vary significantly across reporting periods. The findings suggest that accountability assessments based solely on program spending ratios may obscure underlying financial vulnerabilities. The paper concludes by discussing implications for nonprofit governance, donor decision-making, and regulatory oversight.

title: Information Overload Under Rational Learning
affiliations: , Virginia Tech and Virginia Tech - Department of Economics

detail.title: Information Overload Under Rational Learning
detail.abstract: We study how rational agents can perform worse when more information is available. An agent observes a (d+1)-dimensional signal vector and chooses a learning rule to estimate an unknown state. The agent trades off a quadratic prediction error with a processing cost that depends on both the rule and the complexity of the information environment. We define information overload as an increase in inaccuracy in the optimal mean squared error beyond some finite complexity threshold. Despite having access to unlimited information, we show that if (i) constant (prior-based) rules are costless, and (ii) any sequence of nondegenerate responsive rules becomes too costly as complexity increases, then optimal behavior eventually defaults to a prior-based constant rule, thus establishing necessary and sufficient conditions for overload to occur under rational learning. We also characterize the structure of optimal inference under overload, and apply it to correlation neglect and social learning.

title: Front-Running the Red Carpet: A Measurement Study of Media Torrent Leaks and User Risks
affiliations: University of Oklahoma - Data Science & Analytics Institute, University of Oklahoma and University of Oklahoma - Data Science & Analytics Institute

detail.title: Front-Running the Red Carpet: A Measurement Study of Media Torrent Leaks and User Risks

declarations.funderStatement: Self-funded project via lab internal funds.

detail.abstract: We study how streaming service fragmentation (SSF) causes media access friction (MAF), providing a catalyst for audiences to acquire their desired media through illicit channels. This friction is fueled by the current exclusivity model employed by the large streaming platforms. Decentralized, peer-to-peer (P2P) protocols like BitTorrent, through its trackerless DHT, present a robust illicit distribution channel. We introduce a cross-layer design that links the supply of torrents available via the BitTorrent DHT with the diffusion mechanics of specific torrent swarms around the release of new titles. Our macro panel (n=1,469 titles) shows that each additional legitimate provider of a given title reduces the instantaneous hazard of a first torrent by about 4.2%. In the micro panel, we tracked 244 torrent swarms involving 167,607 unique peer IPs across 220 physical jurisdictions and 7,277 ISPs. We find the torrents follow Scurve diffusion with sharp and short-lived first mover advantage, where activity is highly concentrated by jurisdiction and network. Pre-release windows show elevated risk to users, with one-third of torrents carrying suspicious executables. Because BitTorrent operates as a federation of title-centric micro-networks with no stable chokepoints, enforcement techniques such as domain takedowns, CDN de-peering, or broad Layer-3 blocking are blunt and ineffective for this distribution channel. This paper shows that the more durable lever is to reduce MAF at its source: multihoming more titles and loosening exclusivity may temper early leaks, attenuate early diffusion, shrink early swarms, and lower user cyber risk relative to efforts that target the P2P layer itself.

title: The Thermodynamic Efficiency Inversion: A Comparative Energy Lifecycle Assessment of Generative AI Inference versus Ad-Supported Web Search Sessions

detail.title: The Thermodynamic Efficiency Inversion: A Comparative Energy Lifecycle Assessment of Generative AI Inference versus Ad-Supported Web Search Sessions
detail.abstract:
The dominant environmental narrative surrounding Generative AI frames each large language model (LLM) query as an energy-intensive event, vastly more costly than a traditional web search. This paper challenges that framing through a full-stack, session-level Comparative Energy Lifecycle Assessment (CELCA). While server-side LLM inference does exceed a simple search-index lookup, the meaningful comparison is between complete user sessions aimed at satisfying the same complex information need.

When the system boundary expands to include data transmission over mobile networks, client-side rendering of media-rich webpages, and the energy overhead of the programmatic advertising supply chain — costs that LLM responses entirely bypass — the calculus inverts. Drawing on Google's peer-reviewed production measurement (arXiv:2508.15734; 0.24 Wh/prompt), Nokia's 4G energy intensity data (0.17 kWh/GB), HTTP Archive 2025 page-weight benchmarks (2.56 MB median mobile), and CHI '25 experimental task-completion data (Spatharioti et al., 2025), we construct three scenarios supported by a Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis.

The central finding is that for complex synthesis tasks on a mobile connection, an LLM session consumes approximately 4–9× less energy than an equivalent ad-supported web search session. This advantage disappears on Wi-Fi for simple queries, and reverses for reasoning-model and agentic workflows. The Jevons paradox, hallucination penalty, and embodied carbon asymmetry are rigorously addressed.

title: Continuous Judgment and the Responsibility Field
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Continuous Judgment and the Responsibility Field
detail.abstract: This paper presents a process-based, axiomatic framework for interpreting religious concepts such as free will, judgment, mercy, and salvation through systems-oriented reasoning. Central to the model is the Responsibility Field, defined as a global, time-distributed structure generated by free human choices and their consequences. Judgment is reformulated as continuous directional orientation rather than a final verdict, while heaven and hell are understood as instantaneous states of alignment. Mercy is modeled as non-retaliatory action that dampens systemic divergence. The framework preserves genuine free will while rejecting punitive metaphysics and deterministic convergence. It is offered as a philosophical model rather than a doctrinal proposal, aiming to bridge religious intuition and contemporary systems thinking.

title: Beyond the Checkbox: Categorization Ambiguity and Career Trajectories of Multiracial Workers
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Beyond the Checkbox: Categorization Ambiguity and Career Trajectories of Multiracial Workers
detail.abstract: Multiracial workers face a hiring-gate penalty that disappears once they are employed. Using longitudinal workforce data spanning over one billion profiles (2000–2024), I find that in U.S. states with large Asian populations, multiracial workers are hired into positions 0.1 seniority levels lower than comparable White workers (p < .001), but advance at identical rates once employed. This penalty survives education controls, does not vary by occupational context, and has been stable for 25 years. The pattern—concentrated where evaluative information is scarcest and absent where performance records are available—is consistent with a categorization ambiguity mechanism: when perceivers cannot assign someone to a single racial group, the evaluative process detaches from standard scripts, producing a penalty at the point of hire that individuating information later overrides. I develop a theory of categorization ambiguity as a potentially distinct axis of workplace inequality, arguing that the consequences of failed racial categorization are channeled through gender. Suggestive descriptive evidence from 76.5 million person-year observations is consistent with this gendered account: multiracial men outpace White men in career seniority while multiracial women fall behind White women, and multiracial career outcomes exceed any weighted average of monoracial groups. These descriptive patterns require individual-level controlled estimation to establish robustness; the hiring-gate finding, which uses individual-level data with regression controls, provides the paper’s primary empirical contribution. The paper challenges the categorical architecture of diversity research—discrete groups, mutual exclusivity, unambiguous assignment—by showing that for the fastest-growing U.S. demographic, it is the difficulty of classification itself, not group membership, that shapes career outcomes.

title: Beyond Moore's Law: Strategic Decoupling and the Dissolution of the NVIDIA Regime in the AI Era
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Beyond Moore's Law: Strategic Decoupling and the Dissolution of the NVIDIA Regime in the AI Era

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants or animals, and therefore ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: The AI revolution has been dominated by NVIDIA's co-evolutionary ecosystem, which combined GPU hardware with CUDA software to establish a formidable technological regime. This paper explores the gradual dissolution of that regime through the lenses of Hegelian dialectics and Williamson's Transaction Cost Theory. NVIDIA's dominance rests on a Dual Strategy of Open-Closed: CUDA was opened as a de facto standard to attract developers and expand the ecosystem, while core competencies remained closed to secure monopolistic rents. This duality created high human asset specificity and prohibitive switching costs, effectively locking the industry into NVIDIA's governance. However, the physical limits of Moore's Law have triggered a Value Chain Pivot, a structural axis shift from monolithic GPU design toward heterogeneous integration and advanced packaging. In parallel, Strategic Decoupling represents the deliberate maneuvering of hyperscalers, memory suppliers, and manufacturers to circumvent CUDA and reclaim architectural sovereignty. While the Pivot reflects an inevitable structural transformation of the global value chain, Decoupling embodies intentional strategic artifice-remaining within NVIDIA's ecosystem for immediate scale while simultaneously building CUDA-free alternatives. Together, these dynamics erode NVIDIA's encapsulation and usher in a multipolar order centered on On-site Adaptive Innovation, where contextual responsiveness and integration define the new competitive advantage in the post-Moore era.

title: The Influence of Price and Promotion on MSME Product Sales with Halal Certification as a Moderating Variable
affiliations: Universitas Islam Negeri Mataram and Universitas Islam Negeri Mataram

detail.title: The Influence of Price and Promotion on MSME Product Sales with Halal Certification as a Moderating Variable
detail.abstract: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) play a significant role in Indonesia's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and employment absorption. However, MSMEs often encounter difficulties in boosting sales amid intense competition, particularly when it comes to effective marketing strategies such as pricing and promotional efforts. Additionally, the increasing awareness among Muslim consumers regarding halal products has made halal certification a critical factor influencing purchasing decisions. This study aims to examine the impact of price and promotion on MSME product sales, with halal certification serving as a moderating variable. This quantitative research employed a Likert scale questionnaire for data collection and Partial Least Squares (PLS) for data analysis. The findings reveal that price does not significantly affect product sales, with a P-value of 0.312 > 0.05, indicating that price fluctuations are not the primary determinant of sales. On the other hand, promotion has a significant impact on product sales, with a P-value of 0.000 < 0.05, demonstrating that promotional activities can directly lead to an increase in sales. However, halal certification does not moderate the relationship between price and sales, with a P-value of 0.202 > 0.05, nor does it moderate the relationship between promotion and product sales, with a P-value of 0.469 > 0.05.

title: KPI-Driven In-Flight Catering: Enhancing Passenger Experience
affiliations: and Islamic Azad University Science and Research Branch

detail.title: KPI-Driven In-Flight Catering: Enhancing Passenger Experience
detail.abstract: This study investigates the pivotal role of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) in optimizing in-flight catering services, aiming to enhance both the passenger experience and operational efficiency within the airline industry. Recognizing the complexity and strategic importance of catering management, the research employs a mixed-methods approach, integrating quantitative data from airline operations and qualitative insights from industry stakeholders, including catering managers, cabin crew, and passengers. Through comprehensive analysis, the study identifies essential KPIs across service quality, operational efficiency, cost management, sustainability, and innovation, demonstrating their substantial impact on improving catering services. Case studies from leading airlines provide practical examples of successful KPI implementation, underscoring the adaptability and effectiveness of KPI-driven strategies in addressing diverse operational challenges and passenger needs. The findings contribute to both theoretical frameworks and practical applications in airline catering management, offering actionable recommendations for airlines to implement robust, data-driven approaches to enhance in-flight dining experiences. By leveraging targeted KPIs, airlines can achieve greater customer satisfaction, operational excellence, and competitive advantage, aligning catering services with evolving passenger expectations and industry standards.

title: Avoiding Cargo-Culting and Communication Silos in Digital Media Systems

detail.title: Avoiding Cargo-Culting and Communication Silos in Digital Media Systems

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no financial, personal, or professional relationships that could be perceived as influencing the research reported in this paper. The study was conducted independently, without external sponsorship or institutional direction.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve clinical interventions, medical experimentation, or vulnerable populations. The research is based on organisational analysis and practitioner-oriented inquiry. No personal identifiers or confidential data were collected. Accordingly, formal institutional ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The study was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract:
This research analyses how cargo-culting practices and communication silos shape digital media content management workflows within already under practiced contemporary organisational contexts. Drawing on organisational communication theory, platform studies, and sociomaterial perspectives, the study reframes persistent digital media management challenges as structural and communicative conditions rather than technical or skills-based failures.

Cargo-culting is conceptualised as the uncritical replication of tools, workflows, and performance indicators based on perceived external success, without contextual understanding of their underlying logic. on the other side, Communication silos are analysed as organisational conditions in which visibility, authority, and interpretation are unevenly distributed across roles, platforms, and workflow stages. The research demonstrates that these two phenomena are mutually reinforcing within platform-mediated digital media systems.

Using an exploratory qualitative research design, the study integrates open-ended practitioner surveys, practice-informed inputs, and workflow and process mapping across agency-based, multi-client, and platform-dependent digital media environments.The Empirical findings reveal consistent fragmentation between planning, execution, and evaluation stages; asymmetric access to platform data and metrics; dominance of platform-defined performance indicators; and widespread reliance on replicative “industry standard” practices under conditions of time pressure and evaluative risk.

Rather than treating digital platforms as neutral tools, the analysis positions them as communicative infrastructures that stabilise siloed visibility and encourage cargo-cult adoption of workflows and metrics. The study argues that platform architectures, role-based access configurations, and metric-centred evaluation systems collectively obscure deeper organisational communication problems, limiting reflexive learning and shared sense-making.

By reframing digital media workflows as communicative systems, this research contributes a research-led, non-prescriptive analysis of why cargo-culting and communication silos persist despite widespread professional expertise and technological sophistication. The study offers an analytically grounded foundation for future research on platform dependency, organisational communication, and digital media governance, without proposing solutionist frameworks or optimisation templates

title: Elevating In-Flight Entertainment (IFE): A Strategic Approach to Performance Optimization
affiliations: and Università degli Studi di Firenze

detail.title: Elevating In-Flight Entertainment (IFE): A Strategic Approach to Performance Optimization
detail.abstract: This study investigates the pivotal role of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) in optimizing In-Flight Entertainment (IFE) systems to enhance passenger experience and operational efficiency within the airline industry. Recognizing the strategic importance of IFE as a component of airline service that significantly influences passenger satisfaction and loyalty, this research employs a mixed-methods approach, integrating quantitative analysis of system usage and engagement data with qualitative feedback from passengers and crew. Through this comprehensive evaluation, the study identifies critical KPIs content diversity, user engagement, system reliability, and customer satisfaction that directly impact the effectiveness of IFE offerings. The findings reveal that a dynamic content strategy, personalized engagement efforts, and a focus on technical reliability are essential for elevating the overall passenger experience. Additionally, the research underscores the necessity of a strategic, datadriven approach to IFE management, enabling airlines to align their offerings more closely with passenger preferences and technological advancements. By highlighting actionable insights and offering recommendations for strategic IFE optimization, this paper contributes valuable perspectives to the ongoing discourse on enhancing in-flight services in a competitive market landscape.

title: A DNA-Based Framework for Growth Forecasting in High-Engagement Durable Goods Sectors

detail.title: A DNA-Based Framework for Growth Forecasting in High-Engagement Durable Goods Sectors
detail.abstract: Predicting the long-term performance of new market entrants is frequently hindered by the high-variance nature of raw engagement data, which often conflates organic interest with ephemeral promotional spikes. This paper proposes a novel framework for growth forecasting based on the synchronization of Signal Floor Isolation and Sector Archetype DNA. The methodology utilizes a rolling 10th-percentile quantile regression to isolate the "Organic Floor"-the unbreakable baseline of a brand's presence-from a limited thirty-day trial period. This identified signal is then mapped against a library of high-fidelity "Sector Archetypes"-established market leaders whose performance data has been decomposed into 48-slot longitudinal seasonality matrices (12 months × 4 marketing weeks). By calculating the Pearson correlation coefficient between the entrant's trial floor and the archetypes' seasonal fingerprints, we identify the most statistically similar market DNA. The model then applies a scaled intensity projection to bridge temporal gaps and forecast the entrant's annual organic potential. Finally, we introduce the concept of Channeling Requirements, a mathematical derivation used to calculate the specific campaign reach needed to bridge the deficit between predicted organic performance and defined stakeholder targets. This approach transforms early-stage market analysis from speculative estimation into a data-driven strategic roadmap.

title: Does Teaching Entrepreneurship Produce Entrepreneurs?

detail.title: Does Teaching Entrepreneurship Produce Entrepreneurs?
detail.abstract: I examine whether undergraduate entrepreneurship education increases business formation, exploiting the staggered introduction of entrepreneurship programs at over 150 U.S. universities. Using newly assembled data linking historical university catalogs to LinkedIn career histories for more than 300,000 graduates, I implement a within-university, adjacent-cohort difference-indifferences design. Program introductions reduce immediate business formation by 7.5 percent, with no effect on long-run entry or firm survival. Text-based classification via a large language model indicates the decline is driven by small-business entry, with no offsetting increase in growth-oriented entrepreneurship. These findings suggest university entrepreneurship education has limited effectiveness as a policy tool for stimulating new business creation or survival.

title: European Companies Operating in China: From Digging in to Rethinking their Presence
affiliations: Bruegel, Bruegel and Bruegel

detail.title: European Companies Operating in China: From Digging in to Rethinking their Presence
detail.abstract: We use nearly a decade's worth of panel data from European Union Chamber of Commerce in China business confidence surveys to analyse the deteriorating outlooks of EU firms in China from 2017 to 2025. All firms in China currently face challenges including slow profit growth and deflation. These circumstances have contributed to a rare drop of foreign direct investment into China over the last two years. However, certain challenges are particularly acute for foreign firms, including those from the EU. According to survey results, business sentiment among EU firms operating in China has never been bleaker. Respondents view their profitability, growth opportunities and competitiveness negatively, while fewer respondents than ever plan to expand their Chinese operations. Moreover, significant shares of respondents report recent increases in political pressure from the Chinese state and media, while nearly a third of respondents say they are siloing their Chinese operations, meaning separating them from other global activities. Disaggregated by size, sector, and years of operation in China, insightful differences emerge between the business strategies of EU firms. We broadly classify these into four categories: doubling-down, hedging, hibernating and ready to exit. EU policymakers should consider how to address the challenges EU firms in China face, such as asset-heavy sectors being 'stuck' in China and smaller firms lacking the capacity to operate at a loss in China's market. The EU might need to facilitate transitions for these companies, helping them to reduce exposure to China and diversify into other emerging markets.

title: India-China Rapprochement: What are the Long-Term Prospects?
affiliations: University of Delhi and Bruegel

detail.title: India-China Rapprochement: What are the Long-Term Prospects?
detail.abstract:
China-India relations, which have long been fraught, were further complicated by the 2020 military standoff on the Himalayan border. The political disruption had a significant impact on Chinese companies’ presence in India. And yet, India’s dependence on Chinese imports has increased since.

The Indian economy is decelerating at a challenging time for Prime Minister Modi, who governs in a coalition. China could offer a partial solution to India’s economic woes by providing manufacturing FDI and creating jobs. The Modi-Xi ‘rapprochement’ after their encounter at the October 2024 BRICS summit signals that relations could improve. India may be willing to accept targeted investment from China, but relations are unlikely to fully normalise, particularly since the 2025 India-Pakistan military stand-off. 

There are three main reasons for this. First, the Indian army remains cautious about the situation at the border and security risks relating to China. Second, the United States under President Trump will exert pressure on Modi not to depend further on China. This is even more relevant in the context of Trump’s threat to impose tariffs on India. Third, Indian public opinion on China and the Belt and Road Initiative remains negative. 

India is predicted to experience greater growth than China in the coming decades, meaning China could lose its upper hand in economic relations between the two countries. This, however, will depend on how dependent India becomes on China for imports or for jobs through FDI and other channels. The militarised border, India’s asymmetric economic dependence on China and China’s leadership in the Global South will still shape the relationship even if the Indian economy grows to a similar size to China’s. India-China ‘rapprochement’ is possible but will remain fragile and is unlikely to be maintained in the long run.

title: G7-Led International Financial Framework for Digital Governance

title: Radical Novelties in Critical Technologies and Spillovers: How do China, The Us and The Eu Fare?
affiliations: Bruegel, Bruegel and Bruegel

detail.title: Radical Novelties in Critical Technologies and Spillovers: How do China, The Us and The Eu Fare?
detail.abstract: Critical technologies including artificial intelligence, semiconductors and quantum computing are attracting attention because of their indispensable nature and their role in national security strategies. We compare China, the United States and the European Union in these technologies and their subfields. We use large language models (LLMs) to identify which patents in these technologies can be considered most groundbreaking (not patented before) and worth replicating. These are 'radical novelties.' We find that the US clearly dominates quantum. Chinese and EU progress is similar. The US does slightly better than China in AI with clear dominance in generative AI, but China stands out in some important subfields, such as aerial vehicle technology. China dominates in a larger number of semiconductor fields but not in the highest value added, which is related to design. In a second step we assess how quickly radical novelties in these three technologies are transferred from one economic area to another and within each economic area. We find that the fastest transmission overall is for AI. The EU is by far the slowest in replicating radical novelties from the US and China, while the US and China tend to replicate European novel patents relatively quickly. Radical novelties are also replicated quickly between China and the US which is surprising given US controls on exports of critical technologies to China. Our findings are concerning for Europe because it does not produce enough critical patents in these technologies and because it is slower in replicating patents from the US and China.

title: Will China's Economy follow the Same Path as Japan's?
affiliations: Bruegel and Bruegel

detail.title: Will China's Economy follow the Same Path as Japan's?
detail.abstract: Since the bursting of China's real-estate bubble in mid-2021, there has been a growing concern that the Chinese economy could end up like that of Japan in the early 1990s. Some structural patterns are strikingly similar: low private consumption over a long period, especially when compared to the rest of the world, and an excessively high savings ratio, though China's imbalances now are even larger that Japan's were then. Initial policy responses to the bursting of their respective bubbles have also been similar. Both China now and Japan then were initially hesitant to ease monetary and fiscal policies, and opted to expand manufacturing, with an eye on external demand, supported by more research and development expenditure. In both cases, the outcomes were stubborn trade surpluses and a mercantilist attitude to their growth problems, leading to the United States taking protectionist measures. China also seems to be following Japan's offshoring of production to mitigate the impact of protectionism. The main difference, though, is that China now is a poorer country than Japan was then, with still more convergence opportunities ahead. China is also a much bigger military and geopolitical contender than Japan ever was. China's geopolitical weight is behind the US technological containment of China, but also gives China more room for manoeuvre globally, especially in the Global South. It remains unclear-though globally significant-whether China will be able to deviate from the path followed by Japan in the 1980s and 1990s.

title: Cat Food Communists and the Politics of Securities Regulation
affiliations: DePaul University College of Law

detail.title: Cat Food Communists and the Politics of Securities Regulation
detail.abstract:
The Securities Act’s private offering exemption allows companies to sell their securities without having to go through the expensive and time-consuming process of registering the sale with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”).  Largely due to this exemption, the amount of capital raised privately dwarfs the amount raised publicly every year.  But despite the private offering exemption’s significance, the Supreme Court has only spoken once on its scope.  A single case from the 1950s, SEC v. Ralston Purina, requires investors to be sophisticated and have access to information for a sale of securities to qualify as a private offering.  Yet no scholar has ever undertaken an in-depth study of this case’s history and background.

This article seeks to fill that void.  Through archival research in the papers of Supreme Court Justices, Ralston the company, and its executives, this article documents an alternative narrative for a seemingly run-of-the-mill case.  Led by a maverick founder and chairman, animal and pet food company Ralston took the radical step of allowing even its most working-class employees to buy and own company stock.  This choice—to let the workers own their own company, and therefore the means of production—came to the Supreme Court in the height of McCarthy-era fears about communism.  The resulting decision, which allowed to Ralston to continue selling stock to its sophisticated executives (read: the bourgeoisie), but not to rank-and-file employees (read: the proletariat), can and should be read alongside contemporaneous cases like Dennis v. United States and Garner v. Board of Public Works as part of the Supreme Court’s anticommunist cannon.

This new understanding of Ralston leads to three important implications.  First, in a time where agencies’ rulemaking power is in flux—and challenges to rules seem more likely to succeed without Chevron deference—the statutory basis for what is effectively our entire system of securities regulation should have firm footing.  The current Court believes the words of a statute matter and is willing to jettison past readings that lack a textual basis.  Ralston is just such a case; it may be subject to challenge.  Second, this article’s new understanding of Ralston shows that a period’s zeitgeist can have long-term legal effects, not only in areas of constitutional law that we frequently associate with such eras, but also in seemingly mundane statutory matters, where an interpretation is forced to meet the moment.  Finally, Ralston teaches that securities regulation is about who a society will allow to own a business and therefore the means of production.  This inquiry is an inherently political one, encompassing possibilities from total government ownership to ownership by private individuals.  But which private individuals will be allowed to own businesses is also part of the analysis, and that question has distributional consequences for society.  The paper concludes by tying Ralston to the executive branch’s recent attempts to acquire corporate control and the ongoing pushback against stakeholder capitalism.

title: Universal Basic Income, Degrowth, and the Transformation of Work: Insights from Dynamic Macro-simulation
affiliations: University of Antwerp, Humboldt University of Berlin and University of Freiburg

detail.title: Universal Basic Income, Degrowth, and the Transformation of Work: Insights from Dynamic Macro-simulation
detail.abstract: As the poly-crisis deepens and welfare states confront intersecting ecological, economic, and social challenges, calls for a post-growth rethinking of work and welfare are gaining momentum. Among the most debated proposals stands Universal Basic Income (UBI), often framed as an eco-social transformation pillar. UBI promises to decouple subsistence from employment, reduce precariousness, and enable shorter working hours – all features which resonate with degrowth imaginaries. Yet, critical questions remain about its fiscal feasibility, distributive impacts, and environmental implications within a contracting economy.,This study investigates whether, and how, UBI could operate as a fiscally viable, eco-socially coherent policy under degrowth trajectories. It draws on two complementary dynamic macro-simulation tools: EUROGREEN and a custom-built Python-based system dynamics model. Together, these models explore the interaction between UBI, progressive and ecological taxation, labour, and carbon emissions in France, with particular attention to work quantity and quality, time use, and unpaid care.,Simulation results indicate that UBI consistently reduces inequality and cushions household incomes in both growth and degrowth contexts, without inducing large-scale labour withdrawal, while enabling time reallocation towards unpaid care, leisure, and socially valuable non-market activities. However, its employment, fiscal, and environmental effects depend strongly on the surrounding policy mix. Under degrowth, UBI alone does not guarantee favourable outcomes, but can contribute to socially coherent transitions when combined with working-time reduction and progressive ecological taxation. Across both models, emissions reductions are driven primarily by structural and energy-related policies rather than by UBI itself.

title: The Race Between Technology and Sobriety: Distributional Pathways to Planetary Sustainability
affiliations: University College London and University of Geneva

detail.title: The Race Between Technology and Sobriety: Distributional Pathways to Planetary Sustainability
detail.abstract: This paper introduces a novel application of the Kaya identity to assess the roles of technological change and consumption behaviour in shaping global greenhouse gas emissions. Drawing on numerical insights from counterfactual emission reduction scenarios, we quantify the adjustments in technology and consumption required to remain within the carbon budget by 2050 and explore their distributional implications. Building on this analysis, we develop a simple analytical model that formalizes the resulting carbon budget trilemma: under binding ecological constraints, rising consumption, technological progress, and widening inequality cannot sustainably coexist. We place these transformations in historical perspective by examining a set of precedents - from wars and epidemics to economic collapses and episodes of rapid technical upgrading - that provide comparative magnitudes for the scale of change implied by a binding carbon budget. Our conclusions unveil a race between technological innovation and consumption sobriety to reach planetary sustainability, in which global inequality acts as a boundary constraint. Given past technological progress, and current levels of global inequality, it is unlikely that sustained reductions in average consumption can be avoided if we are to respect ecological constraints.

detail.abstract: This paper challenges the standard economic theory applied within empirical literature on housing allowances for rent. The arguments challenged are (i) subsidy is a price drop which increases demand, (ii) allowance is income, where housing is a normal good, which raises demand, (iii) higher subsidy increases willingness to pay more for housing, and (iv) allowance incentivises optimal consumption to their highest achievable value. In practice, tenants remain unaware of price discounts for the distribution of rents, rendering revealed preference/demand theory inconsistent. Not incomes, allowances (in New Zealand) unfold as a(regressive) negative income and wealth tax unique to each recipients resources.

title: Policy design or disinformation: Which is the key to US climate policy support?
affiliations: University of Victoria, University of Victoria and University of Victoria, School of Public Administration

detail.title: Policy design or disinformation: Which is the key to US climate policy support?
detail.abstract: Many researchers argue that efficient and fair climate policy designs are key to achieving support for climate policies. However, behavioural and political scientists suggest that citizens are largely unaware of policy designs, and are subject to discursive strategies designed to reduce support for climate policy. Existing research has not explicitly compared the relative role of policy designs and discursive factors in predicting public support for different types of climate policies. Using a representative survey of American citizens (n=2,500), we attempt to close this gap. Our objectives are to assess: (1) levels of support for different types of climate policies in the US and by region; (2) perceptions of climate policy costs, stringency, sequencing, and cost of inaction; and (3) the relative role of climate policy designs versus climate delay discourses in climate policy support. We find that policy design features and discursive factors are both important predictors of support for climate policy, and that support for voluntary climate policies is greater than for compulsory policies in the US. The exception to this rule is renewable energy regulations, which receive high support from the US public despite being compulsory. Our results have implications for the design and communication of effective climate policy in the US, and suggest the need for further research into the impact of elite fossil-fuel discourses on global climate delays.

title: Implicit Tax Rates and Marriage
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Implicit Tax Rates and Marriage
detail.abstract: Federal income tax law reform has reduced traditional statutory marriage penalties, but many working-age households now face steep implicit marginal tax rates from incomeconditioned programs. This paper shows that Affordable Care Act premium subsidies and income-indexed student loan repayment obligations create implicit marginal rates that materially affect marriage and childbearing incentives. Using numerical examples under current law, it demonstrates that income aggregation for subsidy eligibility and repayment calculations can eliminate premium tax credits and sharply increase required payments, producing effective marginal rates that in some ranges substantially exceed statutory tax rates. The modern marriage penalty therefore arises less from the income tax brackets and more from the interaction of stacked AGI-linked programs. Revisiting eligibility cliffs, discontinuous rate jumps, and nonindexed thresholds could reduce these distortions.

title: Mortgage Credit Supply Shocks and House Prices: Structural Evidence from New Zealand

detail.abstract: New Zealand's housing unaffordability crisis is widely attributed to supply shortages, migration, or falling interest rates. This paper shows instead that it is primarily a credit-driven phenomenon. Using quarterly data from 1998Q4-2025Q1, we estimate regime-specific structural VARs that identify credit as the initiating shock. Across all regimes-pre-COVID, QE-inclusive, and post-GFC-credit shocks permanently raise house prices and explain up to 70-80% of their medium-run variance, while price-to-credit effects remain negligible. Flow-based measures of new mortgage credit confirm that short-lived lending bursts operate as overlays on a persistently leveraged balance-sheet stock. Together, the results indicate that New Zealand's housing cycle is structurally organised around bank balance-sheet expansion rather than income, population, or interest-rate fundamentals.

detail.abstract: This study analyzes the effects of working from home on land rents and fertility. To this end, we developed a monocentric urban economic model incorporating household fertility choices. When the urban population is considerably small, the equilibrium with working from home cannot be sustained. As working from home becomes available, the land rent curve flattens, increasing regional fertility rates. Furthermore, as the urban population increases, land rents increase, fertility rates decline, and the proportion of households choosing to work from home increases.

title: Stress-Testing Proposals to Add Autism Claims to the Vaccine Injury Compensation Program

detail.title: Stress-Testing Proposals to Add Autism Claims to the Vaccine Injury Compensation Program

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I declare that I do not have any personal or financial relationship with any person or organization that has or could be perceived to have influenced this paper.

detail.abstract:
HHS Secretary Kennedy may soon propose to expand the National Vaccine Injury Compensation Program to compensate claims for some constellation of the conditions usually found in the Autism Spectrum Disorder. Recently, his "close policy advisors" have specifically raised the prospect of revising the portion of the VICP Injury Table which currently covers certain specified encephalopathies, but which also expressly excludes such clinical features classic to ASD.

Under the Vaccine Act, such a decision to revise the Injury Table to include some new type of claim rests with the Secretary. But it will then be subject to judicial review under the Administrative Procedures Act, based on whatever record is compiled during a six-month period of public comment mandated by the Vaccine Act.

One critical issue in that review will be whether any such revision of the Injury Table will promptly bankrupt the VICP. Opponents of such an expansion can certainly argue that it would be the epitome of an "arbitrary and capricious" administrative act to add so many autism claims that they would destroy the entire Program. 

As we explained in a prior article, about 16,000 American children are diagnosed with "profound" autism each year.; the VICP typically awards petitioners with similar significant cognitive deficits about $2 Million per case; and hence an expansion of the VICP that covered just those profound cases would require more than $30 Billion in additional awards, Moreover, the immediate docket of such claims would be at least $100 Billion -- and more likely $250 Billion. It is thus clear that if some future Table revision captures even 2% to 5% of the children with profound autism, the Trust Fund would quickly disappear.

In this article we consider how HHS could, and should, stress-test the financial burden of any such revision of the Injury Table, using data already available to HHS, most notably its Autism Developmental Disabilities Monitoring Network (ADDM), which includes the records of children who were both diagnosed with profound autism and who also had some history of seizure. That latter fact is critical because a seizure is the event which currently drives VICP compensation. 

We then outline the issues that will arise if HHS alters one or more of the other key components in the current Injury Table provisions on encephalopathies, which require that the seizure (1) be documented as sufficiently severe; (2) occurred within a short specified time after one of two types of vaccinations; and (3) not be the likely result of one of a number of enumerated alternative causes. We consider how even apparently small changes to those terms could "capture" so many cases of profound autism that the VICP would almost certainly be overwhelmed. And for those reasons, we argue that HHS should commit now to undertake such a stress test -- and publish both the results and underlying data -- to allow outside experts, and the public at large, to confirm or refute those results before the proposed revision is advanced through the brief period for public review and comment.

detail.abstract: This chapter discusses the relationship between Jewish Law and Hasidism – the religious revival that began in Eastern Europe in the second half of the eighteenth century and that continues to animate Jewish politics, religion, music, storytelling, and practice to this very day. Literary sources of Jewish law are presented and the hasidic contribution to each legal genre is detailed. This is followed by an overview of the state of research, and the contention that this fertile ground remains to be fully explored. The chapter concludes with a case study of hasidic headwear – fur hats known as shtrayml, spodik, or kolpik – and how they are treated in the writing of Rabbi Hayim Elazar Shapira of Munkács (1871-1937), known by the title of his collection of responsa: Minhat Elazar. The shtrayml case study highlights the potential of Jewish legal writing from the hasidic milieu.

title: A Martingale Optimization Method Based on Volatility Adaptation to Improve Trading Strategies in the Indian Market
affiliations: ,  and

detail.title: A Martingale Optimization Method Based on Volatility Adaptation to Improve Trading Strategies in the Indian Market
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether the Indian equity market follows a Martingale process and, based on such statistical behaviour, how to design an optimal trading strategy. Through econometric tests of the NIFTY 50 Index of the daily closing prices of the market between November 2024 and November 2025, we test the efficiency and predictability of returns in the market through econometric tests, such as the ADF, KPSS, LjungBox, Variance Ratio, ARIMA and GARCH tests. The results demonstrate that NIFTY 50 returns are linearly unpredictable, uncorrelated serially, and steady, which is consistent with the Martingale Difference Hypothesis. Conversely, volatility clustering and a slight deviation from a random walk are signs of conditional inefficiency. Therefore, while the Indian market is weak-form efficient, optimization strategies based on volatility can yield better performance.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces UNC System L, a structural architecture that reframes global financial dynamics by shifting the analytical focus from macro-level indicators to the micro-level psychological tension experienced by individuals. Traditional economic systems rely on inflation, interest rates, liquidity and volatility as primary metrics. UNC System L replaces these with a Quad-Core Flow Architecture-Flow Capacity Index (FCI), Human Stability Buffer (HSB), Systemic Flow Equalizer (SFE), and Invisible Load Index (ILI), and introduces a new concept absent from all existing economic, psychological and systemic models, Elasticity of Perceived Abundance (EPA). EPA represents the capacity of a population to perceive abundance independently of real resources. This paper argues that economic reality is generated by perception rather than the reverse, and that systemic stability emerges from architectural flow rather than monetary control. The framework provides a new foundation for understanding tension, interdependence and behavioral thresholds in advanced financial systems.

title: A Model Framework for Automating the Recruitment Process

detail.title: A Model Framework for Automating the Recruitment Process
detail.abstract: Recruitment processes are labor-intensive and susceptible to human bias. This paper introduces a model framework to automate key recruitment stages, with a focus on objectively assessing candidate-culture fit. We design a model that quantifies key organizational culture traits, and we validate their dependencies using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). Our SEM results suggest an adequate model fit, indicating that cultural compatibility may be an important factor in predicting successful hiring outcomes. Our framework offers a novel approach to recruitment automation by integrating culture fit analysis, thereby enhancing the alignment of new hires with the organization's values and practices.

detail.abstract: This paper evaluates whether U.S. public companies should be required to disclose the number and percentage of shares registered outside the Depository Trust Company’s nominee, Cede & Co., including directly registered, non-Cede-owned (NCO) shares. The analysis identifies a regulatory blind spot in current SEC disclosure rules and explains how rising NCO ownership can reduce market transparency by distorting common measures of tradable supply and short-selling conditions, including public float and short-interest ratios. Drawing on a review of SEC disclosure requirements, issuer-level evidence from recent market episodes, transfer-agent practices, and state corporate-law inspection rights, the study uses case examples—GameStop, AMC, Express, Bed Bath & Beyond, KOSS, and Trump Media & Technology Group—to illustrate how undisclosed NCO ownership can affect investors’ and analysts’ interpretation of liquidity and lending supply. The paper argues that because NCO shares are typically illiquid and unavailable for securities lending, omitting them from Forms 10-K and 10-Q can materially misstate market-liquidity metrics when NCO ownership becomes significant. It proposes targeted amendments to Regulation S-K to standardize issuer reporting of NCO shares, with the goal of improving float measurement, enhancing the interpretability of liquidity data, and strengthening investor protection.

title: Eastern Mind, Western Technology: How China Harnessed Foreign Knowledge to Achieve Technological Supremacy

detail.title: Eastern Mind, Western Technology: How China Harnessed Foreign Knowledge to Achieve Technological Supremacy

detail.abstract: This thesis examines how China leveraged foreign knowledge to achieve technological supremacy, framing the phenomenon through the concept of the "Eastern Mind, Western Technology." Unlike Western liberal norms, which assume openness, reciprocity, and the universal dissemination of knowledge, China has historically distinguished between soft knowledge (culture, philosophy, diplomacy) and hard technical knowledge, which is strategically guarded and integrated into longterm state planning. Drawing on historical precedents from classical Chinese statecraft and the selective adaptation of Indian Buddhism by Faxian and Xuanzang, the study demonstrates the continuity of China's civilizational approach to knowledge absorption. The analysis traces multiple mechanisms of technological acquisition, including state-directed programs (e.g., the 863 and Torch initiatives), diaspora returnees trained abroad, joint ventures with foreign firms, and controlled knowledge transfer. By comparing China's approach with Western liberal frameworks and other Asian cases such as Japan, South Korea, and India, the thesis highlights how cultural epistemology, language, and institutional strategy enabled China to adapt, rather than simply adopt, foreign technology, converting international openness into a coherent national advantage. The work concludes that China's rise in areas such as semiconductors, artificial intelligence, and advanced manufacturing reflects a deliberate, multi-generational civilizational strategy, offering lessons for understanding the interplay between culture, state policy, and global technological competition.

title: Metaphysical Semiotics and Conservative Demonology: The Darkness of Science

detail.title: Metaphysical Semiotics and Conservative Demonology: The Darkness of Science
detail.abstract: Science rarely circulates as method alone. It travels through moral cosmologies, symbolic hierarchies, and ontological commitments that exceed empirical procedure. In certain conservative discursive formations, scientific knowledge does not appear simply as evidence or explanation but as a sign, one capable of signaling inversion, corruption, hubris, or even spiritual displacement. Light/darkness, sacred/profane, and truth/deception binaries provide the semiotic architecture through which epistemic disagreement migrates into metaphysical antagonism. Climate change skepticism, anti-evolution rhetoric, artificial intelligence anxieties, and bioethical controversies illustrate how institutional authority can be re-coded as ontological threat. In such contexts, science is narrativized less as mistaken than as morally misaligned. Drawing on semiotic theory, sociology of knowledge, and modernity theory, the analysis traces the mechanisms through which inversion, conspiracy framing, purity language, and apocalyptic horizon-setting stabilize this recoding. A reflexive turn complicates the picture by asking whether scientific modernity itself generates forms of metaphysical dislocation that render such symbolic reactions intelligible. What emerges is not a defense of science nor a critique of conservatism, but an account of how epistemology becomes ontology, and how knowledge, under specific moral conditions, is rendered as darkness.

title: Myanmar's Neutrality: Blessing, Burden, Or Impossible Ideal?
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Myanmar's Neutrality: Blessing, Burden, Or Impossible Ideal?
detail.abstract: Myanmar’s idea of neutrality isn’t as simple as just “staying out of it.” For a small country  between China and India, neutrality has often been a matter of survival. It is careful balancing act, shaped by decades of internal struggles and political upheaval. Sometimes, Myanmar has pulled back, retreating inward to protect its own sovereignty. Rather than following a strict rulebook of non-alignment, Myanmar has developed its flexible strategy,  that allows it to adapt to changing circumstances. For Myanmar, neutrality isn’t passivity. It’s a shield, and a survival tool, a way for a small country to keep its footing amid the unpredictable currents of global power.

title: Max-Min Bilinear Completely Positive Programs: A Semidefinite Relaxation with Tightness Guarantees
affiliations: , Hong Kong Baptist University and The Hong Kong Polytechnic University

detail.title: Max-Min Bilinear Completely Positive Programs: A Semidefinite Relaxation with Tightness Guarantees
detail.abstract: Max-min bilinear optimization models, where one agent maximizes and an adversary minimizes a common bilinear objective, serve as canonical saddle-point formulations in optimization theory. They capture, among others, two-player zero-sum games, robust and distributionally robust optimization, and adversarial machine learning. This study focuses on the subclass whose variables lie in the completely positive (CP) cone, capturing a broad family of mixed-binary quadratic max-min problems through the modelling power of completely positive programming. We show that such problems admit an equivalent single-stage linear reformulation over the COP-CP cone, defined as the Cartesian product of the copositive (COP) and CP cones. Because testing membership in COP cones is co-NP-complete, the resulting COP-CP program inherits NP-hardness. To address this challenge, we develop a hierarchy of semidefinite relaxations based on moment and sum-ofsquares representations of the COP and CP cones, and flat truncation conditions are applied to certify the tightness. We show that the tightness of the hierarchy is guaranteed under mild conditions. The framework extends existing CP/COP approaches for distributionally robust optimization and polynomial games. We apply the framework to the cyclic Colonel Blotto game, an extension of Borel's classic allocation contest. Across multiple instances, the semidefinite relaxation meets the flat-truncation conditions and solves the exact mixed-strategy equilibrium.

detail.abstract:
This study examines the multifaceted dynamics of colonial rule in Africa by synthesising insights from scholarly articles that explore the historical, social, and political implications of colonialism. Researchers adopted a structured approach, gathering and analysing qualitative data from a wealth of online literature sources and expert opinions. They meticulously selected 36 peer-reviewed articles spanning from 1951 to 2022, each discussing the Dynamics of Colonial Rule in Africa. The data revealed the limitations of the growth of uncertainty to govern institutions in African countries. The systematic approach ultimately provided valuable insights into the struggles and challenges faced by African leaders to sustain the Dynamics of Colonial Rule in Africa. It argues that colonial rule was not a monolithic experience but rather a complex interplay of forces that varied significantly across different regions and cultures. The research highlights how colonial powers implemented diverse administrative strategies ranging from direct governance to indirect rule that had profound and lasting impacts on local societies. By analysing key themes such as economic exploitation, cultural imposition, and resistance movements, the study underscores the systemic inequalities established during colonialism that continue to influence contemporary African states. Furthermore, it investigates the role of local actors, including traditional leaders and resistance movements, in shaping the colonial experience and the post-colonial landscape. These interactions reveal a dynamic relationship between colonisers and the colonised, challenging simplistic narratives of domination and submission.

The findings illuminate the continuing legacy of colonial rule in African governance, emphasising the need for a nuanced understanding of how historical injustices resonate in contemporary conflicts and inequalities. Ultimately, this study contributes to the discourse on colonialism by offering critical insights into the complexities of Africa’s past and its implications for current and future trajectories in on the continent. By contextualising colonial experiences, it aims to enhance discussions surrounding post-colonial identity, sovereignty, and social justice in Africa today.

detail.abstract: Incident duration refers to the length of time an incident persists on the roadway, from its onset to full resolution. Prolonged incidents can cause secondary crashes, congestion, and reduce network efficiency. This study investigated the impact of active traffic management systems, specifically, Lane Control Signs (LCS) and Variable Speed Limit (VSL) on the duration of traffic incidents along major expressway corridors. Using a Double Machine Learning (DML) Causal Inference framework, the research aimed to quantify the effects of these interventions on incident clearance efficiency across different incident types. The model estimated Average Treatment Effects (ATE) for treated segments equipped with VSL or LCS, compared to matched control sites. Extensive data preprocessing, feature engineering, and subgroup analysis were conducted, and the Conditional Shapley Value Index (CSVI) was integrated for proper confounder selection. The analysis revealed that interventions yielded more substantial reduction in incident duration, particularly for high-severity events and during peak traffic periods. VSL demonstrated comparatively greater effectiveness than LCS. Subgroup results highlighted the varying effectiveness of treatments by event type like crashes, disabled vehicles, and abandoned vehicles and temporal context, indicating that system performance was not uniform across all scenarios. The findings offered actionable insights for transportation agencies to prioritize deployment of VSL in critical segments and optimize the use of LCS where appropriate. Overall, this study demonstrated the potential of data-driven causal modeling in informing Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) strategies and policy decisions for enhancing roadway resilience and incident response effectiveness.

detail.abstract: Financial institutions often face a critical challenge in the silent failure of Value-at-Risk (VaR) models, whose performance is typically only assessed through ex-post backtesting such as independence and unconditional coverage tests that identifies problems only after significant losses have occurred. To address this gap, this paper introduces the VaR Efficiency Ratio (VER). The ratio compares the VaR estimate from against a distribution-free risk limit derived solely from variance via the Cantelli inequality. title: Decentralization, Crowds, and Cycles: Why Bitcoin's Architecture Makes Booms and Busts Structurally Likely

detail.title: Decentralization, Crowds, and Cycles: Why Bitcoin's Architecture Makes Booms and Busts Structurally Likely
detail.abstract: Bitcoin's recurring boom-bust cycles are widely observed but still debated. Many explanations focus on halvings, speculation, or external shocks. This paper makes a structural claim: Bitcoin's proof-of-work decentralization makes cyclicality persistent and likely because consensus and price formation both depend on large, uncoordinated crowds interacting through a shared price signal. The argument proceeds in three steps. First, decentralization in Bitcoin is an ongoing social process, not a static property: miners, investors, and intermediaries must continuously participate for the system to function. Second, this crowd operates through a feedback architecture in which one protocol-level negative loop (difficulty adjustment) is embedded in at least six market-level positive loops that can amplify shocks in both directions. Third, repeated movement through leverage-fragility dynamics is consistent with Minsky's Financial Instability Hypothesis: apparent crash "causes" are often trigger events acting on pre-existing endogenous fragility. A companion Bayesian scenario analysis shows that three trend specifications with near-identical out-of-sample fit diverge by more than an order of magnitude at long horizons, quantifying structural uncertainty. The paper's conclusion is probabilistic rather than deterministic: Bitcoin's architecture is not guaranteed to oscillate under every parameterization, but it is structurally cycle-prone.

detail.abstract: The NBA draft lottery is intended to promote competitive balance by infusing weaker teams with young cost-effective talent. Yet the current system suffers from a linear race to the bottom wherein the losingest teams retain the best odds of receiving a high pick. Recent reforms have flattened lottery odds but have not eliminated strategic losing. This paper proposes a tiered draft lottery mechanism designed to interrupt the race to the bottom while better allocating the very best players to some of the losingest teams. Under the proposed system, lottery teams are grouped into three tiers (1-5, 6-10, 11-14) based on regular-season losses, with different pick ranges allocated probabilistically by tier (1-2, 3-5, 6, 7-8, 9-14). The mechanism introduces upward competitive pressure at the bottom of the standings by making moderate improvement non-punitive and, in some scenarios, materially valuable. We analyze expected draft positions, risk profiles, and behavioral incentives across tiers, and compare the proposed system to the current NBA lottery structure. The proposal illustrates how targeted incentive design-rather than full randomization or strict record-based assignment-can better align late-season competition with league objectives.
